tuning_key.text: The credibility of what we know / Strains for authenticity
tuning_key.attribution: Chords of Truth — Lucid Principles Canon (CC BY 4.0)

context_block: Right now, something in you knows the difference between what you're pretending to believe and what you actually know to be true — and that difference is the only real boundary you have. The strain you feel isn't weakness; it's the signal that authenticity is trying to become real. Today, stop smoothing it over. Let the line be sharp.

practice.title: Locate the Strain
practice.instruction: Notice one place in your body where you feel the pull between what you're saying (or thinking) and what you actually know — throat, chest, gut — and name it silently without fixing it.

practice.title: Claim the Clarity
practice.instruction: Ask yourself: "What do I know that I haven't said?" and let the answer arrive without judgment, then feel how your body responds to that truth being acknowledged, even silently.

practice.title: Hold the Line
practice.instruction: Breathe into that clarity for three cycles, and then play the echo audio — let the frequency anchor what you just claimed as yours.

archetype_tunings.The Steward: Today's boundary signal arrives as clarity in your operations: what belongs in this system, and what doesn't. The credibility of your stewardship strains toward authenticity—each decision, each delegation, each boundary you hold makes the family's infrastructure more real. Let the line you draw be sharp enough that everyone knows where the coherence begins.
archetype_tunings.The Merchant: Your numbers are a language of boundaries. Today, the signal is precise: what price holds integrity, what terms are real, what exchange is authentic. The credibility of your commerce strains toward what actually works—not what looks good. Let your clarity cut through the noise so the signal reaches clean.
archetype_tunings.The Builder: The boundary you're tuning today is technical and true: what this system will do, what it won't, where the edge is. The credibility of your implementation strains toward authenticity—each specification, each automation, each line of logic either holds the signal or it doesn't. Build the line so clean that the system knows its own shape.

Let the clarity of your signal be sharp enough that the family knows exactly what's real in the field.
